experiment_description: Room-temperature photoluminescence spectroscopy was performed on optically active defects in hexagonal boron nitride. Two drops of solvent-exfoliated hBN solution were drop-cast onto a marked silicon substrate and annealed at 850 °C under a 1 Torr argon atmosphere in a tube furnace, then cooled naturally to room temperature. A custom confocal microscope excited a selected defect using a continuous-wave 532 nm laser, focused with a high-NA objective; fluorescence was collected through the same objective, pump light was suppressed with a long-pass filter, and the emission was routed to a spectrometer. The spectrum was recorded over the visible emission band to identify the zero-phonon-line emission and its spectral width.

zero_phonon_line_center_nm.description: Center wavelength of the zero-phonon line measured from the hBN defect photoluminescence spectrum.

single_photon_emission_bandwidth_nm.description: Reported optical bandwidth of the hBN single-photon emission used for comparison with wavelength-scanned laser excitation.

experiment_description: A single hBN defect emitter was characterized at room temperature by fiber-based Hanbury Brown–Twiss interferometry. The defect was excited with a 100 µW, 532 nm laser in a custom confocal microscope. Photoluminescence was separated from the pump using a 550 nm dichroic beam splitter, filtered with a 20 nm bandpass centered on the emitter zero-phonon line, coupled into a fiber-based HBT setup, and the second-order autocorrelation was normalized to the long-delay value. The autocorrelation trace was fitted using a three-level-emitter model to extract the antibunching value at zero delay and the excited-state decay lifetime under the stated excitation conditions.

second_order_autocorrelation_g2_0.description: Zero-delay normalized second-order autocorrelation of the hBN emitter, reported without jitter correction.

excited_state_lifetime_above_saturation_.description: Excited-state lifetime extracted from the three-level fit to the autocorrelation data; reported uncertainty in the paper is ±0.1 ns.

experiment_description: Anderson localization of hBN single photons was measured in the bulk of a one-dimensional disordered femtosecond-laser-written waveguide array in fused silica. The photonic chip was fabricated in Corning 7980 fused silica using 800 nm, 150 fs pulses at 100 kHz focused 200 µm below the surface with a 20×, NA 0.36 objective; the written waveguides had an index contrast of about 5×10^-4 and elliptic modes of roughly 9 µm by 13 µm. The disordered array contained 101 nominally identical waveguides with off-diagonal coupling disorder: nearest-neighbor coupling coefficients were designed to be uniformly distributed with mean κ0 = 0.08 mm^-1 and disorder ratio Δ/κ0 = 0.8, where Δ is the half-width of the uniform coupling distribution. Single photons from the hBN defect were generated by 100 µW, 532 nm excitation, collected in a confocal microscope, separated from pump light with a 550 nm dichroic, filtered around the zero-phonon-line emission, and injected by free-space optics into waveguides near the center of the disordered array, beginning at waveguide 30 of 101 to avoid edge reflections. The excitation site was shifted to neighboring waveguides to sample 30 disorder realizations. For each realization, the output end facet was imaged with a single-photon-sensitive EMCCD camera, the peak intensity in each output waveguide was extracted, and profiles were shifted to a common launch-site coordinate and averaged. The averaged output profile was fitted to I(j)=I0 exp[-2|j-j0|/ξ], where j is output waveguide index, j0 is the injected waveguide index after alignment, I0 is the fitted central intensity scale, and ξ is the effective localization length in waveguide-site units.

bulk_single_photon_localization_length_s.description: Effective exponential localization length extracted from the disorder-averaged bulk single-photon output intensity profile; reported uncertainty in the paper is ±0.55 sites as a 95% confidence interval.

experiment_description: Boundary Anderson localization of hBN single photons was measured in the same type of one-dimensional disordered fused-silica waveguide lattice. The laser-written chip contained 101 nominally identical waveguides with off-diagonal coupling disorder, coupling mean κ0 = 0.08 mm^-1, and disorder ratio Δ/κ0 = 0.8. Single photons emitted by the room-temperature hBN defect under 100 µW, 532 nm excitation were collected, spectrally filtered around the zero-phonon-line emission, and coupled by free-space optics into the edge waveguide of the disordered array. The output end facet was imaged using an EMCCD camera. The edge-excitation measurement was repeated for four disorder realizations, and the resulting end-facet intensity profiles were averaged. The averaged edge profile was fitted to I(j)=I0 exp[-2|j-j0|/ξ], where j is output waveguide index, j0 is the boundary launch-site index, I0 is the fitted edge intensity scale, and ξ is the effective localization length in waveguide-site units.

edge_single_photon_localization_length_s.description: Effective exponential localization length extracted from the averaged edge-excitation single-photon output intensity profile; reported uncertainty in the paper is ±2.66 sites as a 95% confidence interval.

experiment_description: Wavelength-dependent classical-light localization was measured in the bulk of the same disordered one-dimensional waveguide array to compare with the hBN single-photon result. A filtered supercontinuum laser with optical bandwidth below 4 nm was coupled into central waveguides of the disordered lattice. The laser center wavelength was set successively to 607, 612, 617, 622, and 627 nm. For each wavelength, 30 disorder realizations were sampled by shifting the excitation to neighboring waveguides, the output end facet was imaged, peak waveguide intensities were averaged after aligning the launch sites, and each averaged profile was fitted to I(j)=I0 exp[-2|j-j0|/ξ], where j is waveguide index, j0 is the aligned launch waveguide, I0 is a fitted intensity scale, and ξ is the effective localization length in waveguide-site units.

laser_localization_length_at_607_nm_site.description: Approximate effective localization length read from the plotted fitted value for 607 nm laser excitation.

laser_localization_length_at_612_nm_site.description: Approximate effective localization length read from the plotted fitted value for 612 nm laser excitation.

laser_localization_length_at_617_nm_site.description: Approximate effective localization length read from the plotted fitted value for 617 nm laser excitation.

laser_localization_length_at_622_nm_site.description: Approximate effective localization length read from the plotted fitted value for 622 nm laser excitation.

laser_localization_length_at_627_nm_site.description: Approximate effective localization length read from the plotted fitted value for 627 nm laser excitation.
